result.title: Hidden Messages Between Diffusion Language Model Agents: Causal Evidence for Latent Communication
result.comment: Accepted at the DiffuLM Workshop at NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: Diffusion language models form answers through a sequence of revisable continuous states, but multi-agent systems usually discard those states and make agents communicate only after decoding text. We ask whether one independent diffusion trajectory can pass a compact hidden message into another and, crucially, whether the receiver uses what that message means. In Hidden Messages, a sender compresses its denoising state into four signed dense vectors; the receiver consumes them while retaining its own context, canvas, and trajectory. Removing a message tests whether the channel matters; replacing it with a message from another example tests whether its content matters. Across controlled tasks, derangement removes a +63.6-point advantage on Tiny-A2D and a +100.0-point advantage on Dream-7B, while targeted substitutions steer the receiver toward the substituted fact. On QASC with the two supporting facts split across agents, matched communication reaches 80.8%, but a wrong-example message lowers accuracy to 46.8%, a content effect of +34.0 points. The surprising result is temporal: one late transfer reaches 87.8%, exceeding four recurrent exchanges by +7.0 points. These experiments provide causal evidence for continuous hidden communication between diffusion-LM agents and show that when information is transferred can matter more than how many times agents exchange it.

AI.brief_summary: 研究独立 diffusion LM 轨迹之间能否用四个带符号稠密向量传递隐藏去噪状态，并通过删除消息、替换为其他样本消息的干预，检验接收方是否真正使用消息内容。结果显示内容替换可定向改变接收方答案，且单次较晚传递优于四次循环交换。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本而非视觉工作，但其连续状态通信、删除/替换式因果检验及「传输时机重于交换次数」的发现，可能为 LVR 中 latent 内容是否被使用、THINK/STOP 与计算分配提供可核查线索。
